title: Unjustified sharpened second law $I\to I_A$ in closed-loop/causal setting (eq. 2ndlaw2)

comments.author: human
comments.body: In §3.1 (eq. `2ndlaw2`) the solution replaces $I=\mathcal I(X;Y)$ by $I_A=\mathcal I(X;A)$ in the generalized second law, justified by 'applying Sagawa--Ueda to the effective measurement outcome $A$.' This is not rigorous. In Sagawa--Ueda the measurement outcome is obtained and *then* fed back. Here $A$ is a **causal, history-dependent, feedback-generated control process that drives the very SDE producing $X$**; treating $\mathcal I(X_{[0,\tau]};A)$ between the entire path and the control as a Sagawa--Ueda mutual information ignores the temporal/causal structure (control at $t$ depends only on the past and *changes* the future law of $X$). The correct object in repeated/continuous feedback is generally a **transfer entropy / directed information** (Ito--Sagawa, PRL 110, 180603, 2013), not $\mathcal I(X;A)$. The inequality $I_A\le I$ does not by itself establish validity of $\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle\le -\Delta F+k_BT I_A$. A re-derivation in the closed-loop setting with explicit hypotheses is required.
